meta.method: Assign each unassigned cause/effect node to an existing package by its ESSENTIAL NATURE, considering polarity.

assignments.node_text: אוֹר, שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִנַּפְשִׁין וְרוּחִין וְנִשְׁמָתִין, וְהוּא אוֹר אֵין־סוֹף
assignments.reason: Ein Sof is the transcendent infinite light that is the ultimate goal toward which the mochin race. Section א states it is 'above nefesh, ruach, and neshamah'. The additions file already identified אמצעא דעלמא (center of the world) as a bechina of Ein Sof and placed it in Package 1. Ein Sof is the object that Keter shields and the mochin pursue -- it is the apex of the intellectual/Crown domain. Its essential nature is the divine light at the summit of the Keter-mochin cluster.

Performing mitzvot with joy is the practical expression of the שמחה (joy) that the additions file placed in Package 2. Section ב frames this as the means by which the Shekhinah is liberated from the klipot: 'כְּשֶׁעוֹשֶׂה הַמִּצְוָה בְּשִׂמְחָה אֲזַי מַעֲלֶה הַשְּׁכִינָה'. Its essential nature is joyful divine service -- the Shekhinah/heart/joy domain in its active, embodied form. It is not a separate domain from joy but joy expressed through the mitzvah.

The joy of the mitzvah is the essential quality of שמחה (already in Package 2) as it manifests within the context of mitzvah-performance. Section ב: 'עַל יְדֵי שִׂמְחַת הַמִּצְוָה נִשְׁלָם הַקְּדֻשָּׁה'. The essential nature is joy -- the heart's proper state -- channeled through the mitzvah. This belongs alongside שמחה, לב, and שכינה in Package 2.

This is a variant phrasing of עשית המצוות בשמחה -- 'when one does the mitzvah with joy'. Its essential nature is identical: the joyful performance of mitzvot, which is the active expression of the Shekhinah/heart/joy domain. Package 2.

assignments.node_id: נשלם הקדשה ומעלה החיות והקדשה שבקליפות בבחינת אחד־עשר סמני הקטרת
assignments.node_text: נִשְׁלָם הַקְּדֻשָּׁה וּמַעֲלָה הַחִיּוּת וְהַקְּדֻשָּׁה שֶׁבַּקְּלִיפּוֹת בִּבְחִינַת אַחַד־עָשָׂר סַמָּנֵי הַקְּטֹרֶת
assignments.reason: This describes the completion of holiness and the raising of vitality from the klipot, likened to the eleven incense spices (ketoret). Section ב connects this directly to the Shekhinah's liberation: the ketoret 'gladdens the heart' (קְטֹרֶת יְשַׂמַּח לֵב), and through this joy the Shekhinah rises from the klipot. The essential nature of this process is the restoration of holiness to the heart/Shekhinah -- the very domain of Package 2. The ketoret is the mechanism by which the Shekhinah/joy reclaims its vitality from the klipot.

assignments.node_id: מעלה השכינה שהיא המצוה שהיא שמחת הלב מבין הקלפות
assignments.node_text: מַעֲלֶה הַשְּׁכִינָה שֶׁהִיא הַמִּצְוָה שֶׁהִיא שִׂמְחַת הַלֵּב מִבֵּין הַקְּלִפּוֹת
assignments.reason: This node's text explicitly names the Shekhinah, the mitzvah, and the joy of the heart -- the three core elements of Package 2. Its essential nature IS the Shekhinah rising from exile. The Torah in section ב chains all three: 'מַעֲלֶה הַשְּׁכִינָה שֶׁהִיא הַמִּצְוָה שֶׁהִיא שִׂמְחַת הַלֵּב מִבֵּין הַקְּלִפּוֹת'. This is the Shekhinah in her aspect of liberation -- squarely within Package 2.

The 'rise of holiness' is the ascent of the Shekhinah from among the klipot. The closing section states: 'עִקַּר עֲלִיַּת הַקְּדֻשָּׁה, עַל־יְדֵי הַשִּׂמְחָה'. The essential nature of this concept is the Shekhinah's restoration to her proper place -- the heart filled with joy. This is the telos of the entire Shekhinah/heart/joy cluster in Package 2.

The annulment of the klipot describes the fate of the klipot themselves. The subject and essential nature of this node is the klipot (קלפות) -- the impure husks of Package 3. Even though the outcome is positive for holiness, the concept being described IS the klipot and what happens to them. The closing section says: 'וְעַל־יְדֵי הַשִּׂמְחָה יִתְבַּטְּלוּ הַקְּלִפּוֹת, בִּבְחִינַת וַיְמַדְּדֵם בַּחֶבֶל הַשְׁכֵּב אוֹתָם אַרְצָה'. The essential nature is the klipot-domain in its aspect of dissolution. Package 3 (evil).
